name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CH16_MATCH_Q01 - Salivary glands and pancreas anatomical locations

questiontext.text:
Match the digestive glands in List I with their respective anatomical locations in List II.

List IList II
A. Parotids(i) Below the tongue
B. Sub-maxillary(ii) Cheek
C. Sub-linguals(iii) Between the limbs of duodenum
D. Pancreas(iv) Lower jaw

Choose the correct match from the given combinations.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Saliva is produced by three pairs of salivary glands situated just outside the buccal cavity, while the pancreas is an elongated compound gland associated with the duodenum.

Step 2: Evaluation of Each Gland
The parotid glands are located in the cheek region, corresponding to (ii). The sub-maxillary (sub-mandibular) glands are situated in the lower jaw, corresponding to (iv). The sub-lingual glands are located below the tongue, corresponding to (i). The pancreas lies between the limbs of the C-shaped duodenum, corresponding to (iii).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Combining these anatomical locations gives the correct pairing: A-(ii), B-(iv), C-(i), D-(iii).

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CH16_MATCH_Q02 - Secretory cells of gastric and intestinal mucosa

questiontext.text:
Match the secretory cells in List I with their respective secretions in List II.

List IList II
A. Mucus neck cells(i) HCl and intrinsic factor
B. Peptic (chief) cells(ii) Mucus in gastric glands
C. Parietal (oxyntic) cells(iii) Proenzyme pepsinogen
D. Goblet cells(iv) Mucus in intestinal epithelium

Choose the correct match from the given combinations.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The mucosa of the stomach contains gastric glands with three major cell types, whereas the intestinal mucosal epithelium contains goblet cells that contribute to succus entericus.

Step 2: Evaluation of Each Cell Type
Mucus neck cells in the gastric glands secrete mucus, matching (ii). Peptic or chief cells secrete the inactive proenzyme pepsinogen, matching (iii). Parietal or oxyntic cells secrete hydrochloric acid and intrinsic factor (essential for vitamin \(B_{12}\) absorption), matching (i). Goblet cells of the intestinal mucosal epithelium secrete mucus for lubrication and protection, matching (iv).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Therefore, the correct pairing is A-(ii), B-(iii), C-(i), D-(iv).

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CH16_MATCH_Q03 - Sphincters and valves of human digestive tract

questiontext.text:
Match the sphincters or valves in List I with the junctions they guard or regulate in List II.

List IList II
A. Gastro-oesophageal sphincter(i) Opening of stomach into duodenum
B. Pyloric sphincter(ii) Entry of faeces from ileum into caecum
C. Sphincter of Oddi(iii) Opening of oesophagus into stomach
D. Ileo-caecal valve(iv) Opening of common hepato-pancreatic duct into duodenum

Choose the correct match from the given combinations.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Muscular sphincters and valves along the alimentary canal regulate the unidirectional flow of food, secretions, and undigested residue between successive compartments.

Step 2: Evaluation of Each Structure
The gastro-oesophageal sphincter regulates the opening of the oesophagus into the stomach, matching (iii). The pyloric sphincter guards the opening of the stomach into the duodenum, matching (i). The sphincter of Oddi guards the opening of the common hepato-pancreatic duct into the duodenum, matching (iv). The ileo-caecal valve guards the junction where undigested matter enters the caecum from the ileum and prevents backflow, matching (ii).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Thus, the correct matching is A-(iii), B-(i), C-(iv), D-(ii).

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CH16_MATCH_Q04 - Digestive enzymes and their specific biochemical actions

questiontext.text:
Match the enzymes in List I with their specific digestive functions in List II.

List IList II
A. Enterokinase(i) Hydrolyses starch into maltose at pH 6.8
B. Rennin(ii) Activates trypsinogen into trypsin
C. Salivary amylase(iii) Digests milk proteins in infants
D. Pancreatic lipase(iv) Breaks down fats into di- and monoglycerides

Choose the correct match from the given combinations.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Chemical digestion relies on specific enzymes secreted in different regions of the alimentary canal, each acting on a defined substrate or proenzyme at an optimal pH.

Step 2: Evaluation of Each Enzyme
Enterokinase, secreted by the intestinal mucosa, converts inactive trypsinogen into active trypsin, matching (ii). Rennin is a proteolytic enzyme found in the gastric juice of infants that helps in the digestion of milk proteins, matching (iii). Salivary amylase hydrolyses about 30 per cent of starch into maltose at an optimum pH of 6.8 in the oral cavity, matching (i). Pancreatic lipase breaks down fats (with the help of bile) into diglycerides and monoglycerides, matching (iv).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Hence, the correct matching is A-(ii), B-(iii), C-(i), D-(iv).

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CH16_MATCH_Q05 - Succus entericus enzymes and their end products

questiontext.text:
Match the enzymes of succus entericus in List I with their respective hydrolytic end products in List II.

List IList II
A. Maltase(i) Glucose + Galactose
B. Lactase(ii) Amino acids
C. Sucrase(iii) Glucose + Glucose
D. Dipeptidases(iv) Glucose + Fructose

Choose the correct match from the given combinations.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The final steps of digestion occur very close to the mucosal epithelial cells of the small intestine, where enzymes of succus entericus convert disaccharides and dipeptides into simple absorbable monomers.

Step 2: Evaluation of Each Reaction
Maltase hydrolyses maltose into two molecules of glucose (Glucose + Glucose), matching (iii). Lactase hydrolyses lactose into Glucose + Galactose, matching (i). Sucrase hydrolyses sucrose into Glucose + Fructose, matching (iv). Dipeptidases hydrolyse dipeptides into Amino acids, matching (ii).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Therefore, the correct pairing is A-(iii), B-(i), C-(iv), D-(ii).

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CH16_MATCH_Q06 - Histological modifications of alimentary canal wall

questiontext.text:
Match the anatomical features of the gut wall in List I with their correct descriptions in List II.

List IList II
A. Rugae(i) Glands present in the sub-mucosa of duodenum
B. Villi(ii) Irregular mucosal folds in the stomach
C. Crypts of Lieberkuhn(iii) Finger-like mucosal foldings in the small intestine
D. Brunner's glands(iv) Crypts formed by mucosa between bases of intestinal villi

Choose the correct match from the given combinations.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The basic four-layered wall of the alimentary canal exhibits regional structural modifications in the stomach, duodenum, and small intestine to perform specialised secretory and absorptive functions.

Step 2: Evaluation of Each Modification
Rugae are the irregular folds formed by the mucosa in the stomach, matching (ii). Villi are the small finger-like foldings formed by the mucosa in the small intestine to increase surface area, matching (iii). Crypts of Lieberkuhn are the crypts formed by the mucosa in between the bases of villi in the intestine, matching (iv). Brunner's glands are the glands located in the sub-mucosal layer of the duodenum, matching (i).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Thus, the correct matching is A-(ii), B-(iii), C-(iv), D-(i).

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CH16_MATCH_Q07 - Sites of absorption across the digestive system

questiontext.text:
Match the regions of the alimentary canal in List I with the substances absorbed there in List II.

List IList II
A. Mouth(i) Water, simple sugars, and alcohol
B. Stomach(ii) Water, some minerals, and drugs
C. Small intestine(iii) Glucose, fructose, fatty acids, glycerol, and amino acids
D. Large intestine(iv) Certain drugs contacting mucosa and lower side of tongue

Choose the correct match from the given combinations.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Although maximum absorption of digested nutrients takes place in the small intestine, limited absorption of specific substances also occurs in the mouth, stomach, and large intestine.

Step 2: Evaluation of Each Site
In the mouth, certain drugs coming in contact with the oral mucosa and lower side of the tongue are absorbed into the lining blood capillaries, matching (iv). In the stomach, absorption of water, simple sugars, and alcohol takes place, matching (i). The small intestine is the principal organ for absorption of final digested products such as glucose, fructose, fatty acids, glycerol, and amino acids into blood and lymph, matching (iii). In the large intestine, absorption of water, some minerals, and certain drugs takes place, matching (ii).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Combining these site-specific absorptive roles gives the correct match: A-(iv), B-(i), C-(iii), D-(ii).

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CH16_MATCH_Q08 - Transport mechanisms in intestinal nutrient absorption

questiontext.text:
Match the absorption mechanisms in List I with their characteristic features and examples in List II.

List IList II
A. Simple diffusion(i) Transport of chylomicrons into lacteals of villi
B. Facilitated transport(ii) Absorption of glucose and amino acids with help of carrier proteins
C. Active transport(iii) Energy-dependent uptake of \(Na^{+}\), glucose, and amino acids against gradient
D. Lymphatic fat absorption(iv) Concentration-gradient passage of small amounts of glucose and \(Cl^{-}\) ions

Choose the correct match from the given combinations.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
End products of digestion cross the intestinal mucosa into blood or lymph via passive, facilitated, active, or lymphatic-vesicular pathways depending on solubility and concentration gradients.

Step 2: Evaluation of Each Mechanism
Simple diffusion accounts for the passage of small amounts of monosaccharides like glucose, amino acids, and electrolytes like chloride ions depending on concentration gradients, matching (iv). Facilitated transport involves absorption of substances like glucose and amino acids with the help of carrier proteins, matching (ii). Active transport occurs against the concentration gradient, requires energy, and absorbs nutrients like amino acids, glucose, and \(Na^{+}\), matching (iii). Lymphatic fat absorption involves incorporating insoluble fatty acids and glycerol into micelles, reforming them into chylomicrons in the mucosa, and transporting them into lacteals, matching (i).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Thus, the correct matching is A-(iv), B-(ii), C-(iii), D-(i).

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CH16_MATCH_Q09 - Digestive disorders and protein-energy malnutrition

questiontext.text:
Match the digestive disorders or malnutrition conditions in List I with their characteristic clinical features in List II.

List IList II
A. Jaundice(i) Reflex action controlled by vomit centre in medulla
B. Vomiting(ii) Protein deficiency without calorie deficiency; extensive oedema
C. Marasmus(iii) Liver affected; skin and eyes turn yellow due to bile pigments
D. Kwashiorkor(iv) Simultaneous deficiency of proteins and calories in infants under one year

Choose the correct match from the given combinations.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Disorders of the digestive system include functional/organ conditions such as jaundice and vomiting, as well as protein-energy malnutrition (PEM) disorders—Marasmus and Kwashiorkor—caused by dietary deficiencies.

Step 2: Evaluation of Each Condition
Jaundice affects the liver and causes skin and eyes to turn yellow due to the deposit of bile pigments, matching (iii). Vomiting is the ejection of stomach contents through the mouth, a reflex controlled by the vomit centre in the medulla, matching (i). Marasmus occurs in infants less than one year in age due to simultaneous deficiency of proteins and calories, matching (iv). Kwashiorkor is caused by protein deficiency unaccompanied by calorie deficiency (in children over one year old) and is characterised by extensive oedema and swelling of body parts, matching (ii).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Therefore, the correct pairing is A-(iii), B-(i), C-(iv), D-(ii).
